title: Right Ctrl Key - Remote Desktop Connection
author: summersbr

judgment.rationale: The issue says a shortcut-based Copilot-key remap fails through a VPN/Remote Desktop connection, but it lacks the remote-client type, operating-system versions, exact mapping, and physical-key control needed to compare it to the established Citrix/virtualization reports.
evidence: The author says the shortcut remap works locally but starts Copilot when connecting to a work computer remotely.
The only comment recommends an external remapper and contains no diagnostic outcome.
No PowerToys version, RDP client/version, remote OS, key-event behavior, or remote-session mode is supplied.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a minimal physical Right Ctrl versus remapped Copilot key comparison in the named remote client before associating this with an existing virtualized-input limitation.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report is insufficiently scoped to identify a PowerToys remapping defect, a Windows RDP redirection setting, or third-party remote-client behavior.

issue_context.summary: A user wants a Copilot-key shortcut remap to act as Right Ctrl in a remote work session, but only states that the mapping works locally and not remotely.
known_information: The issue describes a VPN and Remote Desktop Connection workflow.
The user configured the Copilot key through a Keyboard Manager shortcut.
There is no version, configuration, diagnostic archive, or author follow-up.
inferences: Remote keyboard redirection may treat injected remapped input differently from a physical Right Ctrl key, but the report does not identify the client or prove this.
issue_context.analysis: A direct duplicate or code plan would be speculative. The requested comparison can distinguish the PowerToys mapping boundary from remote-desktop keyboard forwarding without requesting sensitive work-environment details.
initial_investigation: Read the full live issue body and its sole comment.
Compared it with the currently active Citrix remapping report #44650; both concern remote-session handling but name different clients and lack a confirmed shared mechanism.
Searched live PowerToys issues for a direct Copilot-key Remote Desktop duplicate and found none.

information_gaps.information: PowerToys version, exact shortcut mapping, remote client name/version, local and remote Windows versions, and results for physical Right Ctrl versus the remapped Copilot key in the remote session.
information_gaps.why_needed: These facts distinguish an RDP input-redirection limitation from a failure to create or forward the PowerToys remap.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: In a non-sensitive remote test session, use a key tester or a simple Ctrl+C control with physical Right Ctrl and the mapped Copilot key; report only software versions and results, not connection or workplace details.

comment.body: Thanks for describing the local-versus-remote difference. To determine whether this is a Keyboard Manager remap problem or remote-desktop keyboard redirection, please provide the PowerToys version, exact shortcut mapping, remote client and version, and local/remote Windows versions. In a non-sensitive test session, compare physical Right Ctrl with the remapped Copilot key using a key tester or a simple Ctrl+C control and report the two results. Please do not include workplace, server, VPN, or account details.
